keyFindings.text: **Composite answer to Q1.** The rule and the derivation are coherent and functioning; what is not functioning is the expectation of a green fleet-wide `verify`. `verify` is the only consumer of stored-vs-derived equality, it is deliberately not a gate, nothing schedules it, and its derivation changes with every commit that touches a doc — so exit 1 on (nearly) every skill is guaranteed until a skill is two-pass reconciled and then left untouched. The open design question that follows is not "fix verify" but "what property should the stored per-doc version assert?" (feeds Q2–Q4).

(b) `quick_validate.py` / `package_skill.py` reject a malformed or absent version at package time [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md:166]. (c) CI's `skill-doc-frontmatter.yml` runs a different guard (`check-skill-doc-frontmatter.sh`), which checks frontmatter coverage, not version values [SOURCE: .github/workflows/skill-doc-frontmatter.yml:31]. Nothing runs `apply`/`verify` automatically, and even `apply` silently skips a differing value without `--update` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/frontmatter-version.mjs:315]. The "nothing enforces it" half is deliberate, documented under the standard's own heading "What nothing enforces" [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md:170].

keyFindings.text: **The derivation is faithful; the stored values are stale snapshots from earlier mint epochs.** Spot check on `stack-detection.md`: 28 commits touch the path, the engine derives `W=26` and expects 2.2.0.26, while the stored value is 2.2.0.0 — consistent with zero-line/rename commits being discarded by the numstat gate and with no re-apply since mint [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/shared/references/stack-detection.md:1]. Other stored values carry a nonzero `Z` that the current rule seeds to `0` (e.g. `sk-code/README.md` stored 2.2.11.0 vs expected 2.2.0.38) [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md:50]. [INFERENCE: Z-bearing stored values were minted under an earlier layout or are human-set values preserved by `skip-conflict`; distinguishing the two needs `git log -S` on the version line and is deferred.] Anchor-era moves also strand children: stored `1.5.0.x` values against expected `2.2.0.y` show child docs were never re-versioned when the skill anchor advanced [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md:61].

keyFindings.text: **The derivation is self-invalidating by construction because `W` is a git-history function.** For every non-`SKILL.md` doc the engine derives `X.Y.0.W` with `W = min(realEditCount(file), 99)` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/frontmatter-version.mjs:282], where `realEditCount` counts commits with nonzero per-file added+deleted `numstat` after `git log --follow` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/frontmatter-version.mjs:70][SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md:90]. Applying `W` is itself an edit that changes `W`, so one pass never converges; the standard mandates a two-pass apply + amend per skill and says the ordinary case is to apply in the same commit as the content change [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md:98][SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md:106][SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md:120]. Nothing carries that discipline into ordinary editing, so stored-vs-derived drift is the default state.

keyFindings.text: **Consolidated Q5 answer (closure):** no hook, generator, packaging step or CI workflow writes a doc version; the only writer is operator-run `apply` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/frontmatter-version.mjs:445]. Every automated check is presence/format only, at three surfaces: the post-edit gate (skill docs), the package validators (command-run), and CI's coverage guard, which does not know the `version` field exists [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/check-skill-doc-frontmatter.sh:7]. `verify` — the only stored-vs-derived comparison — is invoked by nothing at all. Audit trail: iteration 1 (surfaces named) + iteration 2 (inventory) + iteration 3 (legs source-verified, duplicate-engine claim corrected).

**No hook or workflow invokes the package-time validators; they run only inside the create-skill command flow.** A search for `package_skill|quick_validate` across `.opencode/scripts/git-hooks/` and `.skilled/hooks/` returns zero matches, and the `.github/workflows/` search finds no reference either (only frontmatter-guard comments). Package-time validation happens when an operator or command runs `package_skill.py --check` during skill authoring — never on ordinary doc edits, never in CI, never at commit time. [INFERENCE: based on zero-match searches over the hook and workflow surfaces, plus the command-asset usage lines at .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-skill-auto.yaml:227.]

**The only automatic version check is Row 3 of the post-edit router, and its scope is precisely bounded: skill-tree docs only, presence+format, deduped per skill.** Row 3 fires only when the edited file lives under `.skilled|.opencode` + `skills/` with at least four path segments [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/post-edit-quality/lib/post-edit-router.cjs:198], and only when `isVersionedSkillDoc` accepts the file: `SKILL.md` always; `README.md` only when a sibling `SKILL.md` exists; other docs only when a middle segment maps to a canonical skill scope subtree [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/post-edit-quality/lib/post-edit-router.cjs:131]. It then dispatches `check-frontmatter-versions.sh --skill <name>` with a per-skill dedupe key [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/post-edit-quality/lib/post-edit-router.cjs:204], and the wrapper execs the engine in `gate` mode [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/check-frontmatter-versions.sh:13] — "presence + format only — no git, no manifest" [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/frontmatter-version.mjs:399]. Docs outside skill trees receive no version check at all, and no automatic surface compares stored vs derived.

**The package-time validators enforce version presence and 4-part shape at source level — format only, so they too cannot see stored-vs-derived drift.** `package_skill.py` lists `version` in `REQUIRED_FRONTMATTER_FIELDS` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/package_skill.py:56], hard-errors on a missing version for versioned doc-class files [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/package_skill.py:200], and rejects any value failing `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/package_skill.py:334]. The create-skill command asset states the same contract as "package_skill.py --check hard-fails missing version / non-4-part version / name!=folder" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-skill-auto.yaml:210]. `quick_validate.py` mirrors it for skills: missing version is an error, present values must be 4-part [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/quick_validate.py:255]. Neither script reads git, so both check shape only. (Source-verifies the leg iteration 2 cited only through the standard.)

**The validator entrypoints are symlinks, extending iteration 2's alias pattern — and the same test supersedes the "duplicated engine" claim.** `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/quick_validate.py -> ../shared/scripts/quick_validate.py` and `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/package_skill.py -> ../sk-create-skill/scripts/package_skill.py` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/quick_validate.py:1][SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/package_skill.py:1]. Applied to the engine pair: `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/frontmatter-version.mjs -> ../shared/scripts/frontmatter-version.mjs` and `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/check-frontmatter-versions.sh -> ../shared/scripts/check-frontmatter-versions.sh` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/frontmatter-version.mjs:1][SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/check-frontmatter-versions.sh:1]. There is exactly one physical `frontmatter-version.mjs` (21686 bytes) at the `shared/scripts` path [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/frontmatter-version.mjs:1]; `diff -q` reported "identical" because it followed the symlink. The prior "two copies double the update surface" finding is corrected: the update surface is single, and the repository's convention is symlink aliasing (`.opencode/skills`, `.opencode/agents`, and these script pairs), not duplication.

**CI does exercise the engine — via Python tests, against fixtures, not against repository docs.** `.github/workflows/sk-doc-script-tests.yml` runs on every push/PR to `main` and `skilled/**` and executes `bash .opencode/skills/sk-doc/scripts/tests/run-script-tests.sh` [SOURCE: .github/workflows/sk-doc-script-tests.yml:50-53]. The runner's loop globs `test_*.py` only [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/sk-doc/scripts/tests/run-script-tests.sh:12], dispatching each file through pytest or plain python [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/sk-doc/scripts/tests/run-script-tests.sh:19-22]. One file in that glob, `test_validation_switch.py`, invokes the engine: `frontmatter-version.mjs gate --from-manifest` [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/sk-doc/scripts/tests/test_validation_switch.py:183] and `frontmatter-version.mjs apply --paths` [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/sk-doc/scripts/tests/test_validation_switch.py:205]. Consequences: (a) iteration 2's narrow claim stands — the `.mjs` file `test-frontmatter-version.mjs` is not run by any workflow; (b) the broad gloss "the engine is untested in CI" would be wrong — its CLI modes run on every push; (c) no CI step inspects any real document's stored version, so the Q5 conclusion is unchanged. Recorded as a partial SUPERSEDES of the iteration-2 dead-end text.

**Fresh no-caller re-verification: `verify` and fleet `apply` still have no automated caller.** A non-markdown search for `frontmatter-version` across `.github`, `.skilled/hooks`, `.opencode/scripts` and the sk-doc scripts tree returns only the post-edit router (Row 3, gate mode, presence+format) and test files [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/post-edit-quality/lib/post-edit-router.cjs:38]. No workflow or hook invokes `verify` or an operator-scaled `apply`; the `apply` leg in `test_validation_switch.py` runs against an empty path list inside a test [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/sk-doc/scripts/tests/test_validation_switch.py:205].

**Q5 final inventory, with the CI legs now source-cited:** writers — `apply` only, operator-run; automated checkers — post-edit gate (skill-tree versioned docs, presence+format), package validators (command-run, presence+format), CI coverage guard (five-field contract, version excluded), CI script tests (engine fixtures only); `verify` — no caller anywhere. All three artifacts of this iteration cite the two previously uncited CI surfaces.

**The CI coverage guard is a real wired workflow — and its checked contract still has no `version` field.** `.github/workflows/skill-doc-frontmatter.yml` runs on PRs to `main` and pushes to `main`/`skilled/**` when skill `references/**` or `assets/**` paths change, fails closed if the guard file is missing, and executes `bash "$GUARD" . --coverage` [SOURCE: .github/workflows/skill-doc-frontmatter.yml:28-42]. The guard's header contract remains the five fields iteration 2 read — `version` is not among them [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/check-skill-doc-frontmatter.sh:7-8]. Net: CI does check skill-doc frontmatter coverage, but it cannot see any document's stored version.

**The version field is born from a template literal, not a generator.** The `frontmatter-templates` asset carries literal `version:` values (`1.0.0.0`, `1.7.0.0`, `0.1.2.0`, and similar) as the authoring surface where a document's first version value is typed by hand [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md:411][SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md:476]. With `apply` as the only automated writer [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/frontmatter-version.mjs:445], every version value originates from a template literal or an operator command — never from a pipeline.

**Doc-version drift reduces to a single segment.** Segments X (major) and Y (minor) are inherited from the owning skill's anchor, which is resolved from SKILL.md frontmatter and changelog/v*.md filenames as a filesystem max — no git [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md:63-66] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/frontmatter-version.mjs:177-190]. Z is seeded 0 by design [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md:50]. Only W is git-derived: W = min(realEditCount(file), 99) [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md:51] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/frontmatter-version.mjs:281-282]. Any "stays green" analysis therefore only has to solve for W. (Partially new: the derivation was known from iteration 1; the segment-level reduction is the new frame.)

keyFindings.text: **Q2 answer: for an external author, a doc version can only mean the skill era — and the package already carries it.** The meaningful layer is the skill edition: `SKILL.md`'s version plus the changelog history, the human-curated identity of the release a doc belongs to [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md:49] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md:69-70]; the era semantics are exactly what `Y` documents ("ties the doc to its skill-version era") [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/references/frontmatter-versioning.md:79-86].
